business_scope.primary_industry_name: Franchise Licensing and Syrups Supply Chain for Bubble Tea Chains

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: South Korea (national jurisdiction, non-federal, no sub-state tax distinction)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law with statutory commercial registration and special AML/CFT statutes

Agreement Between the Government of the Republic of Korea and the Government of Japan on the Reciprocal Promotion and Protection of Investment (2003)

Free Trade Agreement Between the Republic of Korea and the European Union (Trade and Investment Chapters)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Act on Reporting and Use of Certain Financial Transaction Information (current consolidated text as amended), articles on customer due diligence and suspicious transaction reporting; Enforcement Decree of the Act on Reporting and Use of Certain Financial Transaction Information; Financial Services Commission regulation on customer identification and transaction review of financial companies; Commercial Act (as amended) articles 19, 23, 289, 292 and 317 on trade names, nominal shareholders, corporate structure and registration; Act on the Real Name Financial Transactions and Guarantee of Confidentiality; Foreign Exchange Transactions Act; Fair Franchise Transactions Act; and the Enforcement Decree of the Commercial Act regarding the register of beneficial ownership information held by financial institutions.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation (Company Registration Certificate of Corporation Establishment)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registry Court of the competent district court of the Republic of Korea
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path: 1) obtain certified registry copy from the court; 2) have the copy notarized by a Korean notary public if certification by seal is insufficient; 3) obtain a Hague Apostille from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea; 4) do NOT apply for consular legalization. For a non-Hague destination state, the parallel path is: notarized registry extract, then MOFA authentication, then consular legalization by the Korean embassy/consulate; no Apostille is added.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Company Registry Particulars and Business Registration Certificate (accepted as Certificate of Good Standing)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registry Court of the Republic of Korea and National Tax Service via Hometax
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path: 1) request current certified registry extracts and current business registration certificate; 2) notarize the signatures of the issuing officers; 3) obtain Apostille from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs; 4) no consular step. For a non-Hague jurisdiction, use MOFA authentication followed by Korean consular legalization; never combine Apostille and consular legalization in the same sequence.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution of the Parent Franchisor Appointing the Incorporating Agent and Approving the Korean Chusik Hoesa Structure
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors of the ultimate parent entity or global franchisor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path: 1) notarize the execution page in the country of origin; 2) attach a certified English translation if the original is not English; 3) obtain Apostille in the country of origin in accordance with the Hague Apostille Convention; 4) present the apostilled resolution to Korean counsel; no Korean consular legalization. If the country of origin is not a Hague member, notarize, then have the Korean embassy or consulate legalize the notarized document; do not add an Apostille.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Articles of Incorporation (equivalent of Articles of Association) of the Chusik Hoesa
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Articles executed in Korea are notarized by a Korean notary; if the Articles must be certified for use in a Hague member state, obtain a Hague Apostille from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. If the receiving authority is in a non-Hague state, follow MOFA authentication and then Korean consular legalization. Apostille and consular legalization are mutually exclusive alternative paths and shall not be chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter for the Parent Franchisor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing commercial bank of the parent company in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path: 1) original letter on bank letterhead under bank seal, signed by two authorized officers; 2) notarize the officers' signatures in the bank's country; 3) obtain Apostille in the issuing bank's country; 4) forward to the Korean receiving bank, which may also require direct SWIFT or telephone verification. For a non-Hague bank country, notarize and then obtain Korean consular legalization; the bank letter must never carry both Apostille and consular legalization.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Prior to the acceptance of any incorporator, shareholder, director or beneficial owner, counsel shall screen each individual and each corporation against the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, the UN Security Council Consolidated List, the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, the UK OFSI Consolidated List, and the Republic of Korea's sanctions designations published by the Financial Information Analysis Institute and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. Counsel shall verify legal name, date of birth, nationality, passport number and residential address, conduct UBO tracing at a threshold of 25 percent plus one share, identify Politically Exposed Persons at domestic and foreign levels, run adverse-media and bankruptcy searches, and obtain a source-of-funds declaration for all capital, franchise royalties and syrup supply-chain payments. Enhanced due diligence and senior management approval are mandatory whenever any screening hit, PEP status, nominee relationship, sanction nexus or unexplained wealth indicator appears.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registry Office (www.iros.go.kr) for corporate name clearance and registry filing, together with the National Tax Service Hometax Portal (www.hometax.go.kr) for the related business registration and tax-use name validation.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The statutory trade name of a Chusik Hoesa must be written in Korean Hangul. The National Court Administration applies a four-tier naming examination: (i) the distinguishing trade-name token must be in Hangul and may include a phonetic transliteration of the commercial brand, such as Boba Tea; (ii) the object clause in the Articles of Incorporation must describe the boba tea franchise and syrup supply-chain business within the permitted ISIC 5610 scope; (iii) the full name must not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered company in the same national registry; and (iv) the mandatory legal-form suffix Chusik Hoesa must close the name. English, Chinese characters or other scripts are not permitted as the sole registered name; foreign-language names may appear only as non-registered secondary trade names for banking and cross-border contract convenience.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the registry examiner rejects the proposed Chusik Hoesa name, the applicant receives a written notice stating the ground for rejection. Within 14 days of receipt, a formal objection may be filed with the district court supervising the registry office, supported by a non-use search certificate, a copy of the rejected name filing, a legal opinion on the trade-name doctrine under the Commercial Act, and a request for de novo judicial review. The court must decide the objection within 30 days, and the applicant may concurrently request a stay of related registration deadlines. If the name reservation lapses before the appeal is resolved, the applicant should immediately re-file the same distinctive token in order to prevent name-squatting; if the appeal is unsuccessful, the applicant may re-file using a new distinctive token without incurring additional court penalties. During the appeal, the registry will not grant priority to a third party for the identical disputed name.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or commercial mailbox is not permissible as the sole registered office for a boba tea franchise and syrups supply-chain Chusik Hoesa. Under the Commercial Act, the Articles of Incorporation must specify a definite place of business, and the National Tax Service requires the business registration to reflect the actual business location used for VAT, payroll, and corporate income tax purposes. Commercial banks applying the Real Transaction Principle and the Real Name Financial Transactions Act will reject a corporate account opening if a site visit confirms only a virtual office. A virtual address may be used only as a supplementary mailing address where a physical warehouse, flagship store, administrative office, or licensed food-beverage facility is separately leased and operated in the Republic of Korea. For the franchise royalty model and syrup supply-chain company, both the Fair Franchise Transactions Act disclosure requirements and the tax authority's documentary audit demand a genuine physical business site.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: The quantified risk of an unannounced physical inspection is 10 to 20 percent per year for a franchisor with a compliant physical office and actual inventory or a flagship store, and 45 to 60 percent per year for a company relying on a virtual office or shared mailbox. Municipal tax inspectors and registry officers may initiate a no-notice site visit when the registered address hosts multiple companies, when VAT refunds or foreign-currency royalty receipts are unusually high, when there is a reported discrepancy between the business purpose and physical activity, or when the lease is short-term and unverifiable. The mandatory inspection checklist includes the original lease agreement, floor plan, utility invoices, business registration certificate displayed at the premises, payroll and national social insurance schedules, franchise agreements, POS transaction summaries, VAT tax invoices, syrup inventory records, and a visible signboard matching the registered trade name. The company must retain a registered business operator and staff at the premises during all business hours to pass any such inspection.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Chusik Hoesa registration duty comprising registration tax and local education surtax on paid-in capital
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Registry Court of the Republic of Korea and local autonomous government (National Tax Service collection system)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Registration Tax Act statutory tariff of 0.4 percent of paid-in capital plus 0.04 percent local education surtax, subject to applicable minimums; calculated on an assumed KRW 100,000,000 authorized capital.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name clearance certificate and certified registry extracts from the Internet Registry Office
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Supreme Court of Korea Registry Office
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Court fee schedule for certified company registry extracts and name-conflict search certificates.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization of Articles of Incorporation and incorporators' assembly minutes
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Notary Fee Act statutory tariff plus supplementary drafting and notarial copies.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/UBO due diligence, OFAC/UN/EU/Korea sanctions screening, PEP checks and adverse-media review
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: External counsel and compliance data provider
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for independent KYC, beneficial ownership tracing, and sanctions database screening packages.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Hague Apostille service for the five mandatory legalization instruments plus certified English translations
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea and/or originating-state competent authority
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: MOFA statutory apostille fee per document plus prevailing market rate for translation, notarization, and courier.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Legal counsel for Stage 1 pre-incorporation due diligence, name clearance support, drafting Articles of Incorporation, and ISIC 5610 business-scope alignment
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for cross-border Korean corporate formation and franchise structuring counsel.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Corporate bank account document package, corporate seal, and signature specimen authentication
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Commercial bank in the Republic of Korea and Korean registry/notary office
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Bank service charge for corporate account opening documentation and corporate seal certificate; not a statutory government tariff.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 1000 as amended), Articles 289 (articles of incorporation), 290 (deposit of subscription price), 295, 300, 317 (incorporation registration), 330 (par value shares), 344 (statutory officers); together with the Registration of Non-Contentious Civil Cases Rules and the Framework Act on Local Taxes for registration taxation.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Registration Division of the District Court having jurisdiction over the domestic registered office (e.g., Seoul Central District Court Commercial Registration Office, Republic of Korea).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Incorporation Registration (beob-in seol-rip deung-gi sincheong-seo) together with the notarized Articles of Incorporation (jeong-gwan), capital deposit balance certificate, consent and acceptance forms for directors/auditor, and corporate seal registration documents.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None by law. The Korean Commercial Act does not prescribe a minimum paid-up capital for a Chusik Hoesa. The incorporators may declare any positive nominal capital amount, but the declared amount must be fully paid-in before filing for incorporation and deposited into a designated pre-incorporation blocked settlement account. The bank-issued balance certificate must accompany the court registration application. Failure to deposit the full declared amount invalidates the registration and the subscribers may claw back the funds only if the registration is abandoned.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FORMAL RESOLUTION NO. 1 OF THE FIRST MEETING OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [COMPANY NAME], A CHUSIK HOESA ORGANIZED AND EXISTING UNDER THE LAWS OF THE REPUBLIC OF KOREA. WHEREAS, on [date], the incorporators subscribed for all initial shares of the company, and the company fulfilled the pre-registration deposit requirement by completing payment of the declared paid-in capital into a specially segregated bank account; and WHEREAS, the company was formed as a stock corporation with limited liability under the Korean Commercial Act; and WHEREAS, the board of directors is the statutory management body responsible for ratifying incorporation matters, selecting banking and registered-office arrangements, and appointing the first statutory officers; NOW, THEREFORE, the board, duly convened with the required quorum, unanimously resolves as follows: 1. Ratification of Share Subscription and Capital. The aggregate issued and subscribed share capital of KRW [AMOUNT], divided into [NUMBER] ordinary shares, is hereby ratified and confirmed. The subscriber list is adopted as the corporate record of shareholders. All subscription amounts are deemed fully paid and non-assessable. 2. Registered Office. The registered office of the company is hereby established at [ADDRESS], Republic of Korea. The Representative Director is authorized to file the registered office address with the competent commercial registration registry and to effect all required notifications. 3. Banking Authorization. The company shall maintain its principal current and foreign-currency accounts at [BANK], with account number [ACCOUNT]. The Representative Director, the Chief Financial Officer, and any one additional director designated in writing are hereby jointly and severally authorized to open accounts, execute banking forms, sign checks, initiate franchise royalty wire transfers, process local point-of-sale settlements, approve supplier payments, and manage electronic banking mandates. No single officer may execute a facility payment exceeding KRW [AMOUNT] without a second authorized signature. 4. Appointment of Statutory Officers. The following officers are appointed: [NAME] as Representative Director and Chief Executive Officer; [NAME] as Director and Chief Financial Officer; [NAME] as Director and Company Secretary; and [NAME] as Auditor, subject to the statutory qualifications set out in the Commercial Act. Each officer accepts appointment and shall perform duties with the care of prudent businesspersons. 5. Execution and Corporate Seal. The corporate seal shall be affixed by the Representative Director or Company Secretary to all registration filings, tax forms, bank mandates, franchise counterparty agreements, and food safety license applications necessary to complete stage-two formation and continuing corporate governance. This resolution is immediately effective, shall be recorded in the corporate minute book, and is binding on all officers, directors, shareholders and successors.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and Notarize the Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Public Notary authorized under Korean Jurisdiction; company name registration check may be performed through the Supreme Court Commercial Registration Network or a certified legal service provider.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the articles of incorporation in Korean. The document must state the corporate name containing Chusik Hoesa or Corporation; the principal business purpose covering boba tea franchise consulting, beverage and syrup production, wholesale trade, warehouse storage, and intellectual property licensing; the total authorized and issued shares; whether shares have par value; the registered office address; the method of giving public notice; and the proposed corporate term. All incorporators and first directors must review and execute the articles, and each page must be signed or sealed. Arrange for authentication before a public notary; the notary will confirm pagination, identities, and legal capacity, and notarization is mandatory for the court registry to accept the articles. After authentication, obtain certified copies for use in subsequent filings.
required_dossiers: Articles of Incorporation draft in Korean
Subscriber list and share allocation schedule
Passports or identity cards of incorporators
Passports or identity cards of first directors
Corporate name reservation or search result
Board acceptance consents of first directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary requests amendments, correct the deficient article clauses on the same day and re-execute before the same notary. If a name conflict is found, submit a new corporate name search and substitute a second approved name; no penalty attaches to a pre-registration name correction.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit Declared Paid-In Capital in a Pre-Incorporation Blocked Account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed commercial bank in the Republic of Korea accepting pre-incorporation deposit accounts for company formation.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a pre-incorporation settlement account in the proposed corporate name, or in the names of all subscribers for the purpose of the company, and deposit the full declared paid-in amount. The bank will issue a balance certificate confirming that the funds are dedicated to incorporation and cannot be withdrawn unless the registration fails. The certificate must identify the company name, subscribers, subscribed amounts, and account number. Where no statutory minimum capital applies, the founders may declare a low amount, but the declared amount must be fully wired before the court registration is filed. Foreign subscribers must complete bank customer due diligence and foreign-exchange verification. Retain the balance certificate and the bank's confirmation of blocked status for submission to the court registry.
required_dossiers: Subscriber list with deposit amounts and wiring references
Passports or identity cards of subscribers
Power of attorney if a representative opens the account
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank blocks the account due to incomplete foreign identification, submit statutory declarations or apostilled passports and re-complete due diligence. If a wire transfer is rejected, correct the account ownership title and return reference and re-run the transfer; the bank will issue a fresh balance certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File Incorporation Registration with the District Court Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Registration Division of the District Court having jurisdiction over the principal office (e.g., Seoul Central District Court).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the incorporation registration application on the standard Supreme Court form and submit the notarized articles, capital deposit balance certificate, director and auditor appointment consents, specimen corporate seal registration, proof of registration tax and education surtax payment, and a completed creditors' notice form where required. The registry examines compliance with the Commercial Act formalities and enters the company in the commercial register. Once registered, request a certified corporate registration certificate and a corporate seal certificate. These certified extracts are the foundational documents for all subsequent tax, bank, and licensing applications. Verify that the exact corporate name, address, capital, and officer names are correctly recorded on the issued shelf copy before leaving the registry.
required_dossiers: Corporate seal registration form and seal specimen
Power of attorney for the filing applicant
Proof of payment of registration tax and education surtax
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a supplementary request, cure the stated deficiency within the prescribed period, usually one week, by filing corrected documents. If the registration is rejected, file a reconsideration or immediate appeal under the Non-Contentious Case Procedure Act, or amend the articles and re-file with a revised fee. Any court fee already paid may be credited to the new filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete Business Registration with the National Tax Service
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: District Tax Office of the National Tax Service (NTS) or the HomeTax online portal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete business registration by submitting the certified corporate registration certificate, the lease or title evidence for the registered and business office, the representative director's identification, and the appropriate business-purpose codes covering food service, beverage and syrup manufacturing, wholesale trade, warehousing, and franchise services. The NTS will issue a corporate business registration number and register the entity for value-added tax, corporate income tax, payroll and withholding. This registration also notifies local tax authorities for property and municipal taxes. After issuance, verify that the electronic tax invoice system has been enabled for franchise royalty receipts and for all supply-chain sales.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of corporate registration certificate
Lease contract or title deed for the business office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the NTS queries the registration, update the lease agreement tenant name or the business-purpose classification and resubmit the amendment through HomeTax. If the address is rejected, present the building occupancy certificate and revised lease to the district tax office; the initial filing date is preserved once the correction is accepted.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open Corporate Operating Bank Accounts and Activate Payment Rails
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Money-laundering compliance desk of the chosen Korean bank and the corporate banking division.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open the final corporate operating account by submitting the certified copy of incorporation registration, the NTS business registration certificate, the corporate seal certificate, the board resolution appointing signatories, and valid identification for all authorized persons. Complete the bank's customer risk assessment and confirm the expected transaction profile, including low-risk franchise royalty wires and local POS settlements. Activate the target payment rails: SWIFT franchise royalty inbound wires, Korean won local transfer services, and debit/card POS acceptance where applicable. Record the signature matrix in the corporate records and ensure no single officer can operate above the approved threshold. Obtain IBAN or account confirmation and a bank-issued power of attorney form for future tax withholding and statutory filings.
required_dossiers: Passports or identity cards of all authorized signers
Lease or occupancy proof for the business site
AML risk questionnaire and beneficial ownership statement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests additional beneficial-ownership information, provide a shareholding diagram and board-approved beneficial owner declaration. If an authorized signer is rejected, substitute another director by supplemental board resolution. If the payment rail provider declines, select the bank's alternate POS processor and execute a revised service agreement.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Food and Drug Safety (MFDS) through the local Si/Gun/Gu food safety administration; Korea Fair Trade Commission for franchise registration; National Fire Agency and local fire station for civil defense and fire clearances.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Food Service Business Report/License for retail boba tea stores; Food Manufacturing and Processing Business Report/License for syrup production and beverage supply-chain facilities; Franchise Business Registration under the Fair Franchise Transactions Act; and warehouse business registration for any third-party distribution center storing food materials.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment of the Republic of Korea, operating through the Korea Environment Corporation (K-eco) and the competent local environmental agency.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: For a typical boba tea syrup manufacturing facility or small warehouse with floor area below 1,000 square meters and industrial wastewater discharge below 30 cubic meters per day, the classification tier is Environmental Registration and the facility is exempt from a Full Environmental Impact Assessment. If the project site exceeds any statutory threshold, such as gross site area over 150,000 square meters, siting inside a protected zone, or handling certain prescribed hazardous wastes, the project will escalate to Prior Environmental Review or Full Environmental Impact Assessment under the Environmental Impact Assessment Act.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: For non-sensitive receiving waters, treated wastewater must meet the effluent standards of the Water Environment Conservation Act, indicative maximums of BOD below 40 mg/L, COD below 40 mg/L, suspended solids below 40 mg/L, total nitrogen below 20 mg/L, total phosphorus below 2 mg/L, and pH between 5.0 and 8.7. Syrup production must use food-grade equipment and may not discharge untreated process wash water. Any on-site boiler or thermal oxidizer must comply with the Air Quality Preservation Act, with indicative limits of dust below 10 mg per normal cubic meter, sulfur oxides below 100 ppm, and nitrogen oxides below 50 ppm. Hazardous waste generated from cleaning solvents or lab reagents must be identified under the Wastes Control Act, stored for fewer than 90 days, transported by licensed haulers, and tracked under the electronic manifest system.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Obtain a fire safety certificate and annual business fire inspection from the local fire station under the Fire Facilities Installation and Maintenance Act; secure a civil defense fire permit for commercial cooking, heating, and syrup production equipment; complete structural load review and occupancy approval from the local building authority; and register a workplace risk assessment with the Korea Occupational Safety and Health Agency under the Occupational Safety and Health Act, covering employee safety training, emergency exits, first-aid kits, boiler and pressure-vessel inspection, and forklift or pallet-truck certifications where applicable.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea; electronic tax and VAT filing portal: HomeTax (www.hometax.go.kr); customs export clearance is administered by Korea Customs Service through UNI-PASS.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Domestic newly formed Chusik Hoesa: complete registration at the Commercial Registry of the relevant Korean district court; file a business registration application with the NTS district tax office having jurisdiction over the registered head office or principal place of business; the NTS will verify the identity and location and issue the 10-digit Business Registration Number, which serves as both the corporate TIN and the VAT registration number; the company or its tax attorney must then activate HomeTax e-Tax Invoice access and cash-receipt registration. For a foreign non-resident entity that maintains a Korean domestic place of business or is otherwise required to report Korean VAT, the foreign company must appoint a Korean tax representative and file the same business registration application with the district tax office exercising jurisdiction over the Korean place of business. Required documents include the foreign entity's certificate of incorporation, articles of incorporation, a board resolution appointing the Korean tax representative, an executed power of attorney, proof of the Korean business address such as a lease agreement, and identification documents; foreign documents must be apostilled or certified with Korean translations where required. There is no economic-presence or revenue threshold; registration is mandatory before the first taxable supply in Korea.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation. A Chusik Hoesa incorporated under the Korean Commercial Act is a domestic corporation under the Corporate Tax Act and is subject to corporate income tax at entity level on worldwide income. It is not eligible for pass-through treatment; distributions to shareholders are treated as dividends and are subject to Korean withholding tax or final taxation as applicable.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. Korean tax law does not provide check-the-box elections, partnership pass-through elections, or hybrid mismatch classification elections. Entity status is fixed by the Commercial Act and the Corporate Tax Act; a limited-liability stock company is always an entity-level taxpayer. The consolidated corporate taxation system is a statutory group filing regime for eligible affiliates, not an entity classification election.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the Value-Added Tax Act of the Republic of Korea
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No exemption or monetary threshold in KRW; every business making taxable supplies of goods or services in Korea is required to register for VAT before commencing business. The only small-business simplification is a designated simplified taxpayer filing calculation available to certain individual entrepreneurs with annual taxable turnover not exceeding KRW 80,000,000; this does not eliminate the registration obligation.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Electronic tax invoice issuance is mandatory for VAT-registered businesses. E-Tax Invoices must be issued on or before the supply date and transmitted to the National Tax Service by the day after issuance through HomeTax, an NTS-certified e-Tax Invoice service provider, or an ERP integration using HomeTax APIs. The NTS operates a central data-matching anti-fraud regime under which e-Tax Invoice data, bank settlement data, cash-receipt data, and export customs declarations are reconciled in near-real-time; there is no physical fiscal stamping, and the HomeTax transmission is the fiscal control step. Late, omitted, or false e-Tax Invoice transmission, and POS consumer sales that should be recorded in the cash-receipt system, carry penalty taxes under the Value-Added Tax Act.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exported goods qualify for 0% VAT under the Value-Added Tax Act when the goods are sold to a foreign buyer, physically exported from Korea under a Korea Customs Service export declaration, and settled in foreign exchange. Qualifying services, including international services and services supplied to and consumed wholly outside Korea by a non-resident, also qualify for zero rating. For the boba tea franchise, exports of syrups and ingredients to overseas franchisees can be zero-rated on a shipment-by-shipment basis if the customs export declaration, transport documents, and foreign exchange receipts are maintained. Franchise royalties and brand license fees invoiced to overseas franchisees may be zero-rated where the franchise or licence services are performed for a foreign business outside Korea and are not connected with a Korean place of business; documentation must evidence the foreign recipient's non-resident status, the foreign location of the service, and the actual receipt of royalty proceeds in foreign currency. Offshore digital services are zero-rated only when the supply-place rules treat the digital service as supplied outside Korea and the service is consumed by a non-resident outside Korea. The zero-rating is claimed on the ordinary VAT return, and the input VAT refund will be subject to NTS documentary verification. Domestic franchise royalties from Korean franchisees for stores located in Korea are standard-rated domestic services at 10%.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration electronically filed with Korea Customs Service through UNI-PASS
Commercial Invoice, Packing List, and Export Sales Contract
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical export from Korea
Foreign Exchange Settlement Certificate or Export Proceeds Receipt Certificate issued by a Korean foreign exchange bank evidencing repatriation of export proceeds

Service export substantiation file for franchise royalties containing the franchise agreement, royalty calculations, the overseas franchisee's non-resident certificate or foreign business registration, and bank wire or remittance receipts
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The National Tax Service may audit zero-rated export claims within the statutory assessment period and will cross-check HomeTax e-Tax Invoice filings, UNI-PASS customs declarations, bills of lading or air waybills, and foreign-exchange bank settlement records. If any required document is missing, false, inconsistent, or the foreign-exchange proceeds are not repatriated by the statutory deadline, the zero-rating is retroactively revoked and the 10% VAT is reassessed from the original return due date, together with interest and penalty taxes under the Framework Act on National Taxes. Intentional fabrication or dishonest omission in export evidence constitutes tax evasion under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act and may lead to criminal fines or imprisonment for responsible directors, employees, or tax representatives. Previously granted VAT refunds are clawed back with interest, and if the export financial flows involve related parties, the NTS may also perform a separate transfer-pricing adjustment on franchise royalties.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK), as the central bank, operating jointly with the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act (FETA); day-to-day implementation, reporting collection, and enforcement are executed through authorized foreign exchange banks and Korea Customs Service.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea maintains a liberal but regulated foreign-exchange system. The Korean won is freely convertible for current-account operations such as export/import trade settlements, royalty fees, dividends, and operating disbursements, provided the underlying economic contract is presented to a registered foreign exchange bank and the transaction is reported through the prescribed surveillance channel. Capital-account transactions, including non-resident equity subscriptions, intercompany loans, and financial investments, may be opened outside Korea if the investor uses an approved or a declaration-based route and executes the necessary foreign investment registration. There is no administrative restriction on the repatriation of earnings from a properly registered Chusik Hoesa; the bank will verify that the dividend source is distributable accumulated profit, that withholding taxes are settled, and that no external debt or excessive trade credit is being serviced. Inward capital movements are subject to source-of-funds diligence, while outward remittances may be paused during emergency stability measures. Overall, KRW is convertible but documentary compliance and reporting are mandatory, making the system administratively stringent rather than punitive.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under FETA and related Foreign Exchange Transaction Regulations, Korean exporters must receive settlement for exports within 18 months from the date of export declaration unless a longer deferred-payment term has been approved by the competent foreign exchange authority or delegated bank. There is no mandatory conversion ratio; export proceeds may be retained in an authorized foreign currency deposit account, re-invoiced for operational needs, or converted to Korean won at the prevailing market rate through a licensed foreign exchange bank. The exporter must submit evidence of receipt to the appointed bank and maintain a supporting trade file for the statutory preservation period.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low viability for primary treasury use. Offshore digital electronic money institutions do not hold a Korean banking license and are not permitted to maintain domestic current accounts, receive KRW in electronic money form, or issue Korean account identifiers for entity clearing under the Electronic Financial Transactions Act. Using an overseas EMI as the main operating account would bypass the legal foreign exchange bank channel, create reporting gaps under FETA, and magnify AML risk. Fintech EMIs may be used only as ancillary channels for non-KRW supplier payments in limited jurisdictions, and even then the treasury legal structure should keep all Korean-source franchise and royalty receipts within an authorized bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical attendance is the default for a non-resident statutory director or authorized signatory. Korean banks generally require the director, the shareholder representative, or a legally authorized agent to appear in person at a domestic corporate banking center with original passport, apostilled incorporation documents, company seal, a foreign-investment notification certificate, and beneficial-owner declarations. Consular proxy opening is not a recognized statutory route; on a case-by-case basis a bank may allow remote setup through an enhanced due-diligence protocol using an apostilled power of attorney, live video identity verification, and forwarding of original documents, but the final signing or an interview is still expected in-branch.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk source of initial paid-in capital from a foreign shareholder, with insufficient proof of legitimate accumulation and possible layering through multiple intermediaries.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apostilled certificate of incorporation of the foreign parent; consolidated audited financial statements for at least two fiscal years; six months of bank statements showing accumulation of the subscription amount; shareholder source-of-wealth declaration; tax clearance certificates from the remitter's jurisdiction; a complete funds-flow diagram from source to Korean bank, including all beneficial owner passports and proof of address.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch between the licensed scope of a boba tea franchise company and royalty payment patterns that may indicate trade-based money laundering or hidden settlement of other obligations.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed master franchise agreement, sub-franchise agreements, and the global franchise disclosure document; royalty calculation methodology and store-level POS sales data; sample royalty invoices and VAT returns; customs declarations for syrup exports and import settlements; an independent accountant's report reconciling franchisee turnover to royalty remittances.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident shareholders and indirect ownership through common-law jurisdictions, creating concern over nominee shareholders, unverified ultimate beneficial ownership, or tax-relevant hidden equity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Group organizational chart identifying every intermediate legal entity; apostilled register of shareholders and certificates of incumbency; leases, employee contracts, and utility bills proving economic substance of shareholders; clear passport copies of all ultimate beneficial owners; tax residence certificates; negative sanctions and PEP screening results with source references.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions/PEP screening alert triggered by a name transliteration, resulting in delayed onboarding and over-boarding concerns.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Packaged screening alerts for all name variants; passport and ID scans showing exact official spelling; relevant sanctions list excerpts and the basis for clearing; legal counsel statement confirming the shareholder is not a sanctioned region entity; CRS self-certification and a personal bank reference letter from an established financial institution.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The inbound remittance must be sent by SWIFT MT103 through an authorized foreign exchange bank using a foreign-direct-investment-related narrative and purpose code under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, with the beneficiary legal name as the Chusik Hoesa. The remitter should advise the bank of the KRW conversion and the capital subscription basis; the foreign exchange bank credits the payment to the designated capital collection account, issues a purchase/inward payment receipt, and the entity completes the foreign-invested company registration before the capital verification certificate is issued by a Korean CPA. No cash declarations are needed for wire transfers, but any physical transport of funds exceeds USD 10,000 must be declared to Korea Customs Service. Following registration, the funds can be converted into a basic KRW operating account and applied toward the company's legal capital and working capital needs.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For global franchise supply chain settlements, use SWIFT MT103 or MT202 direct credit transfers for lower-risk royalty, administrative, and confirmed supplier payments; use Commercial Letters of Credit (MT700) when purchasing syrup, food, and packaging assets where shipment and document control are required; and use Documentary Collections (documents against payment or documents against acceptance) for repeated, reliable counterparties seeking balanced trade risk. All KRW-denominated domestic operational liquidity movements should clear through KFTC rails, while cross-border US dollar and euro disbursements should clear via correspondent banking using the bank's SWIFT BIC. Exporters must record trade details in customs systems, while importers must present duty/tax settlement evidence; the bank's compliance team will require an underlying contract and invoice to release each outgoing payment.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore KRW forward contracts with a licensed Korean foreign exchange bank, supported by verified underlying trade or foreign-currency exposure documents
Offshore Korean won non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) only where the bank has a credible internal policy and the hedge relates to genuinely unhedgeable cross-border exposure
Cross-currency swaps with licensed domestic banks for structural franchise investment or intercompany loan rebalancing
KRX-listed foreign exchange futures for short-term liquid treasury hedges, if the corporate treasury is deemed eligible and has platform approval
Options collar structures combining KRW puts and calls, but only through an authorized foreign exchange bank and strictly backed by balance sheet exposure

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Regular Annual General Meeting of Shareholders and approval of annual financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporate records maintained at the registered office; no direct government filing except for registering director/auditor changes with the Commercial Registry Division of the local District Court
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after fiscal year end; for a calendar-year Chusik Hoesa, the meeting must be held by 31 March
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to convene the annual general meeting is a governance breach under the Korean Commercial Act; directors may be subject to summary fines and any resolution adopted without proper convening procedures may be void or voidable. Shareholders may seek court orders to compel the meeting or remove directors. Persistent non-observance can impair corporate good standing and delay statutory audit approval.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Return and tax base settlement filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) via the HomeTax electronic filing system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a fiscal year ending 31 December: by 31 March of the following year; one-month extension to 30 April applies where the corporation is subject to external audit or legal tax-adjustment approval
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: An unfiled return triggers a surcharge of 20% of the assessed corporate tax amount. Unpaid tax after the statutory due date accrues daily overdue interest at approximately 0.022% per day (about 8.03% per annum). NTS may seize bank accounts, receivables, and assets; chronic non-filing can lead to cancellation of the business registration certificate and criminal prosecution under the Framework Act on Taxes.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Local Income Tax report and payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Head-office municipal or district tax authority under the Ministry of the Interior and Safety
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 30 April following the fiscal year end in the normal case; if the corporate tax return is extended to 30 April, the local income tax deadline is extended to 31 May
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to report or pay local income tax adds an unfiled return surcharge of 10% of the local tax payable. Unpaid amounts attract monthly late-payment surcharges (0.75% for the first month and 1.2% thereafter, subject to a statutory cap of 30%). The municipality may issue compulsory collection orders, seize assets, and restrict issuance of local tax clearance certificates.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Franchise Disclosure Document registration renewal and material-change filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Korea Fair Trade Commission (KFTC), Franchise Business Policy Bureau, via the KFTC electronic filing system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a calendar-year franchisor, the disclosure document must be updated or renewed within 4 months after fiscal year end (by 30 April); any material change in registered franchise matters must be filed within 30 days of occurrence
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Operating with an expired or unregistered disclosure statement may trigger administrative enforcement orders and fines of up to KRW 50 million. Knowingly filing false information can lead to criminal penalties including imprisonment up to 3 years or fines up to KRW 50 million. KFTC may prohibit the franchisor from recruiting new franchisees until the registration is restored.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Foreign investment status change report and foreign-invested enterprise annual operational status reporting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE) via Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Any reportable change in foreign investment registration, including shareholding transfers by non-resident shareholders, must be reported within 30 days; annual operational status, when required under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, is due within the statutory window notified by KOTRA/MOTIE
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file a foreign investment change report may result in administrative fines up to KRW 10 million. Overdue or false reporting may lead to cancellation of the foreign investment registration, loss of foreign-investment tax benefits and incentives, and inability to remit dividends or capital abroad under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent external audit is required under the Korean Act on External Audit and Assurance of Stock Companies when total assets at the previous fiscal year end are KRW 12 billion (approximately USD 9.2 million) or more. It is also compulsory for listed companies, financial institutions, designated public-interest companies, and any company whose securities are registered or offered to the public under the Capital Markets Act. Additionally, shareholders collectively holding at least 3% of issued shares may request an external audit under the Korean Commercial Act. If total assets fall below the threshold, the company may still voluntarily appoint a licensed CPA firm, but no statutory audit is imposed.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Korean International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS) apply to public-interest listed entities and certain externally audited companies; non-public Chusik Hoesa entities may apply Korean Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (K-GAAP) under the External Audit Act. Financial statements must also be reconciled to taxable income through the statutory corporate income tax adjustment return under the Korean Corporate Tax Act.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: South Korea does not currently require a separate annual beneficial-ownership declaration to a general corporate registry for a private Chusik Hoesa. The company must maintain a complete and current Register of Shareholders, and any transfer of shares must be reflected in that register. Where a foreign investor holds shares, the Foreign Investment Promotion Act requires reporting of foreign shareholding transfers or changes to MOTIE/KOTRA within 30 days. The Company also has a duty to maintain, internally, current identification records for beneficial owners for anti-money-laundering purposes and to update those records upon becoming aware of a change. No periodic public UBO filing is separately required for the annual compliance calendar.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24% top marginal national rate, plus 4% local income tax surcharge on national corporate tax, yielding 24.96% combined rate for taxable income over KRW 300 billion (progressive: 9% on first KRW 200 million, 19% on KRW 200m-20bn, 21% on KRW 20bn-300bn, 24% above KRW 300bn)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Foreign-invested enterprises in Free Economic Zones or foreign investment zones may obtain 100% or 50% corporate tax relief for 5 to 7 years under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act. R&D expenditure credits of 20%-40%, job-creation credits, and facility investment credits are available. No patent box regime exists; self-developed boba tea recipes and franchise systems generate ordinary income. Foreign investment incentives require substantive local operations, not letterbox structures.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Tax Standard and Tax Base Return (Form No. 1 of the Korean National Tax Service) filed electronically via the HomeTax/NTIS portal (www.hometax.go.kr)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual, with semi-annual intermediate prepayments for corporations with prior-year tax payable of KRW 10 million or more; the annual return remains the primary filing.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 3 months from fiscal year-end; for a calendar-year basis (January 1-December 31), the return is due by March 31 of the following year. Non-calendar fiscal years must file by the last day of the 3rd month after the accounting year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Business Registration Number (BRN) and local tax registration number assigned by the district tax office.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the 10-digit Korean BRN of the Korean Chusik Hoesa. If newly formed, reference the preliminary registration number issued at incorporation. Do not use the foreign parent's ID; the corporate return belongs to the Korean entity, not the overseas shareholder.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate name, representative director, registered address, industry code (ISIC 5610 / KSIC 56119 for beverage franchise operations), and domestic corporation tax classification.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose the full Korean headquarters address and the tax representative's name if the representative director resides abroad. The non-resident parent's name and country appear in Schedule 12 (foreign investment disclosure), not as taxpayer.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Fiscal year beginning and ending dates, and accounting basis.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Korean Chusik Hoesa must adopt a 12-month fiscal year. Short periods require NTS approval. The foreign parent must align its Master File fiscal year for accurate CbCR reporting.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue from franchise fees, entry fees, continuing royalties, syrup and supply sales to Korean franchisees, and intra-group supply chain revenue.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only revenue attributable to the Korean entity is included. If the franchise contract is signed by the foreign parent and the Korean entity only performs logistics, agency commission is the only revenue. Royalty revenue must be booked at arm's length; do not pass through foreign principal revenue unless legally an agent.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-taxable and tax-exempt income (e.g., statutory dividends excluded under CITA Article 12, capital contributions).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Interest on synthetic intercompany loans or economically artificial income cannot be classified as non-taxable. Foreign-source income of a Korean domestic corporation is taxable in Korea unless treaty-exempt; do not exclude overseas sub-franchise royalties.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total deductions: cost of goods sold for syrup, tapioca pearls, cups and raw materials; wages, rent, depreciation, amortization of franchise rights, marketing, and transfer pricing adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Korean entity must substantiate every expense with valid tax invoices. Bribes to health inspectors and hidden franchisee rebates are non-deductible. Intercompany syrup purchases are deductible only up to arm's length price; excess payments trigger non-deductible transfer pricing adjustments.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable base after all deductions, loss carryforward, and special adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a Korean entity with a permanent establishment, the tax base includes all Korean-source income attributable to the PE. If treaty exemption is claimed for a foreign PE, allocate profits carefully; NTS routinely reallocates full profits to Korean sales and marketing functions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statutory corporate income tax computed at progressive rates before credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The same bracket schedule applies as for domestic entities. Foreign-owned companies receive no preferential rate. If taxable income exceeds KRW 30 billion and the entity qualifies as a 'large corporation', an additional 3% surtax may apply under the Tax Adjustment Act.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits: foreign tax credit, R&D credit, job creation credit, voluntary compliance credit, and interim prepayment credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign tax credits are available only for foreign-source income actually subjected to foreign tax and included in the Korean tax base; the parent's credits cannot be transferred. R&D credits require detailed technical reports and contemporaneous documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net corporate tax payable after credits and interim prepayments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Make payment through HomeTax virtual accounts. If unpaid, NTS issues a demand notice with daily late-payment surcharge. Retained earnings should be reconciled later for remittance decisions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Local income tax surcharge at 4% of the national corporate tax computed in Box 8 after credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The surcharge applies to all Korean-sourced taxable income, even when the representative director resides abroad. It is filed jointly on the same return and is required for maintaining the local business license.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Attachments: certified financial statements, tax adjustments (Schedule 20), transfer pricing forms (Local File summary, Master File reference), royalty WHT statements, foreign tax credit schedule, and DTA relief applications.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The tax representative must attach signed TRC, beneficial ownership certificates, and treaty relief applications for cross-border flows. Use the 'Non-Resident Tax Exemption Application' operational form; missing attachments invalidate treaty relief and expose the entity to full statutory WHT.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers an additional tax of 20% of unpaid corporate tax under FANT Article 47-4; 10% if filed after an NTS notice. Intentional under-reporting or a false return triggers 40% of the understated tax; ordinary underreporting 20%. Late-payment surcharge accrues at approximately 0.022% per day (8% p.a.). Missing transfer pricing documentation attracts KRW 5 million per document, and CbCR non-filing can result in KRW 10 million in fines.
